intro_html: Saag is that deep green, garlicky spinach curry that tastes far more involved than it is. Frozen spinach makes it dead simple, and the bowl stays high protein and cheap per serving. One batch makes 14 servings.
cost_closing_html: About $3.50 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Each of the 14 servings lands around 59g protein for about 565 calories, at roughly $2.33 a bowl.
upsell_html: Deep, savory, and simple, this saag makes healthy eating feel effortless all week long. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: Frozen chopped spinach is cheaper than fresh, lasts forever, and melts right into the sauce.
Buy the chicken breast in a value pack to keep the per serving cost down.
One can of coconut milk is all you need for a creamy base, so no need for cream.
make_it: Add the chicken breast and minced garlic to the crock.
Pour in the tomato sauce and coconut milk.
Cover and cook on low for 6 to 8 hours until the chicken is tender.
Shred the chicken and stir in the thawed chopped spinach.
Let everything heat through for another 20 minutes.

head.description: A high-protein Indian meal prep. Fourteen servings at about 565 calories and 59 grams of protein for roughly $3.50 each (at everyday cost).
